scenes.tts: Can a man get better at something every day, and never remember doing it? One patient did.
scenes.visual: Title fades. A hand holding a pen hovers over a star outline. The question appears beside it.
scenes.narration: Can a man get better at something every day, and never remember doing it? One patient did.

scenes.tts: In 1953, a surgeon removed tissue from the inner part of both temporal lobes of a young man.
scenes.visual: A schematic brain seen from below. The inner part of each temporal lobe shades in, left and right. Labels: 1953; medial temporal lobe, both sides.
scenes.narration: In 1953, a surgeon removed tissue from the inner part of both temporal lobes of a young man.

scenes.tts: Afterwards, the patient known as H M forgot new events within minutes, as soon as his attention moved on.
scenes.caption: Afterwards, the patient known as H.M. forgot new events within minutes, as soon as his attention moved on.
scenes.visual: Large initials H.M. A clock face: an event icon appears, the hand sweeps a few minutes, the icon fades as an attention arrow turns away.
scenes.narration: Afterwards, the patient known as H.M. forgot new events within minutes, as soon as his attention moved on.

scenes.tts: Brenda Milner gave him a mirror drawing task. He traced between two outlines of a star, seeing his hand only in a mirror.
scenes.caption: Brenda Milner gave him a mirror-drawing task. He traced between two outlines of a star, seeing his hand only in a mirror.
scenes.visual: Name card: Brenda Milner, Montreal. The double-outlined star; a pen traces between the lines, the hand seen only in a mirror. The line wobbles, errors marked with red ticks.
scenes.narration: Brenda Milner gave him a mirror-drawing task. He traced between two outlines of a star, seeing his hand only in a mirror.

scenes.tts: Across three days of practice, he improved, much as other people do.
scenes.visual: A plot of errors per attempt falling across Day 1, Day 2, Day 3. Corner label: schematic of the shape, not the original data.
scenes.narration: Across three days of practice, he improved, much as other people do.

scenes.tts: Yet he did not remember having done the task before.
scenes.visual: Above each day on the plot, a speech bubble appears: never done this before.
scenes.narration: Yet he did not remember having done the task before.

scenes.tts: His drawing improved, so something kept a record of the practice. Why could he not tell anyone about it?
scenes.visual: The falling curve glows. A question mark sits beside an empty speech bubble.
scenes.narration: His drawing improved, so something kept a record of the practice. Why could he not tell anyone about it?

scenes.tts: The record showed up only in how well he drew. It was not something he could recall and report.
scenes.visual: The curve stays lit, labelled performance. The empty speech bubble is labelled recall and report, crossed out.
scenes.narration: The record showed up only in how well he drew. It was not something he could recall and report.

scenes.tts: So there were two ways of remembering, and the operation badly damaged only one.
scenes.visual: Two boxes appear side by side. One fades grey, labelled severely impaired; the other stays bright, labelled kept.
scenes.narration: So there were two ways of remembering, and the operation badly damaged only one.

scenes.tts: Memory you can bring to mind and state is declarative. It covers events, and facts about the world.
scenes.visual: The grey box is labelled declarative memory, with sub-labels episodic (a breakfast table with a clock) and semantic (a spider, 8 legs).
scenes.narration: Memory you can bring to mind and state is declarative. It covers events, and facts about the world.

scenes.tts: H M could almost never form new declarative memories.
scenes.caption: H.M. could almost never form new declarative memories.
scenes.visual: A tag on the grey box: New declarative learning: severely impaired. Older facts: largely spared.
scenes.narration: H.M. could almost never form new declarative memories.

scenes.tts: Memory expressed in performance is nondeclarative: skills, habits, priming and simple conditioning. He kept his skill learning.
scenes.visual: The bright box is labelled nondeclarative memory, with icons: a hand, a habit loop, a faster arrow, a tone and blink. Tag on the hand icon only: H.M. kept this: skill learning; the mirror star slides in.
scenes.narration: Memory expressed in performance is nondeclarative: skills, habits, priming and simple conditioning. He kept his skill learning.

scenes.tts: Working memory holds a few items for seconds, like a phone number while you dial. His was normal.
scenes.visual: A third box: working memory, with a notepad and a phone number being dialled. A digit-span bar rises to the normal level. A loop arrow labelled rehearsing keeps the number on the notepad.
scenes.narration: Working memory holds a few items for seconds, like a phone number while you dial. His was normal.

scenes.tts: Now a worry. Perhaps recall tests are simply harder, and any brain damage hurts hard tasks first.
scenes.visual: A difficulty ladder: the recall task sits on a higher rung than mirror drawing. Label: single dissociation, one patient, one failed task.
scenes.narration: Now a worry. Perhaps recall tests are simply harder, and any brain damage hurts hard tasks first.

scenes.tts: What second result would rule out the idea that the failed task was just harder?
scenes.visual: A two-task chart: H.M.'s row reads fail on recall, pass on drawing. An empty second row with question marks.
scenes.narration: What second result would rule out the idea that the failed task was just harder?

scenes.tts: A patient with damage somewhere else, who fails the task H M passed, and passes the task he failed.
scenes.caption: A patient with damage somewhere else, who fails the task H.M. passed, and passes the task he failed.
scenes.visual: The second row, labelled hypothetical reverse case, fills: pass on recall, fail on drawing. Two lines, one per patient, cross between the task columns. The hypothetical label stays visible.
scenes.narration: A patient with damage somewhere else, who fails the task H.M. passed, and passes the task he failed.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea of this lesson. Memory systems are told apart by crossed failures.
scenes.visual: Card: The one idea. Text builds line by line as spoken.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea of this lesson. Memory systems are told apart by crossed failures.

scenes.tts: Damage to one structure impairs task A but spares task B. Damage elsewhere does the reverse.
scenes.visual: Two brain icons with different regions shaded. Under each, a task A and task B pair, one crossed out, reversed for the other.
scenes.narration: Damage to one structure impairs task A but spares task B. Damage elsewhere does the reverse.

scenes.tts: Then weakening one shared capacity cannot explain both. The tasks rely, at least partly, on separable processes.
scenes.visual: A single dial labelled one shared capacity is struck through. Two dials appear on one shared panel, labelled process 1 and process 2. Caption: strong evidence, not proof.
scenes.narration: Then weakening one shared capacity cannot explain both. The tasks rely, at least partly, on separable processes.

scenes.tts: That crossing is a double dissociation. It shows each structure is needed for its task in that experiment, not that the memory is stored there.
scenes.visual: The crossing lines return, labelled double dissociation. Two lines of text: Needed for this task: shown. Where it is stored: not shown, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: That crossing is a double dissociation. It shows each structure is needed for its task in that experiment, not that the memory is stored there.

scenes.tts: Needed, not stored. That is the key to reading every lesion study.
scenes.visual: End card: Crossed failures separate memory processes. Needed, not stored.
scenes.narration: Needed, not stored. That is the key to reading every lesion study.
